items.title: uv tool upgrade - problem with private indexes due to short living credentials
items.reason: Canonical match: astral-sh/uv#8523 tracks `uv tool upgrade` preferring receipt-stored private-index configuration over current user configuration, making refreshed authentication unavailable.

items.title: uv tool upgrade does not authenticate against GitLab private pypi package registry
items.reason: Historical near-match: maintainers confirmed that removing credentials from the receipt and failing to transfer matching credentials from `uv.toml` were bugs.

items.title: Avoid writing redacted credentials to tool receipt
items.reason: This deliberately removed both usernames and passwords from receipt index URLs, establishing that later commands must recover authentication safely rather than persist credential-bearing URLs.

items.title: Respect credentials from all defined indexes
items.reason: Fixed credential transfer for duplicated named/default index definitions, but not the scalar legacy `index-url` precedence used here.

items.title: `uv tool upgrade` says "Nothing to upgrade" when index auth is invalid
items.reason: Exact historical match for the misleading no-op result after private-index authentication fails.

items.title: Promote authentication policy when saving tool receipts
items.reason: Fixed silent no-ops for embedded or environment credentials, but explicitly did not cover keyring-provided credentials.

related.search_scope: Searched authenticated GitHub results across open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Literal searches covered `uv-receipt.toml`, `index-url`, username stripping, `tool upgrade`, `Nothing to upgrade`, 401, and the keyring skip message. Conceptual and fix-oriented searches covered receipt precedence, credential persistence/removal, refreshed private-index authentication, subprocess keyring, and historical fixes. astral-sh/uv#16597 was ruled out because it concerns `uv tool run` with an embedded token; astral-sh/uv#15034 concerns Git source serialization during `uv add`; and astral-sh/uv#6420 concerns an SSH Git username.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#8523 already tracks the same underlying bug: `uv tool upgrade` uses receipt-persisted private-index settings instead of usable current authentication from user configuration. astral-sh/uv#21216 adds a username-only subprocess-keyring reproduction. The named-index fix in astral-sh/uv#14858 and invalid-auth fix in astral-sh/uv#18246 do not cover this legacy `index-url`/keyring combination, so this is not a regression of their covered cases and can be centralized in astral-sh/uv#8523.
summary: astral-sh/uv#21216 is a specific keyring-based reproduction of astral-sh/uv#8523. Historical fixes explain why named indexes and embedded or environment credentials behave differently, while the misleading no-op symptom is documented by astral-sh/uv#18120.
draft_response:
Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This is the same underlying issue as astral-sh/uv#8523. `uv tool upgrade` prefers the `index-url` recorded in the receipt over the current user configuration, while receipt serialization removes URL credentials, including a username without a password. In this case that leaves subprocess keyring without the username it needs, and the failed index queries are then reported as `Nothing to upgrade`.

The equivalent named `[[index]]` credential-transfer path was fixed in astral-sh/uv#14858, and astral-sh/uv#18246 made invalid embedded credentials fail loudly, but that fix explicitly did not cover keyring. Let’s keep the remaining `index-url`/keyring work in astral-sh/uv#8523; your reproduction is a useful concrete case for that issue.
